extracted.intended_audience: Small Business Investment Company (SBIC) licensees, their officers/directors/management, and legal/compliance staff (and SBA examiners)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and standards governing SBIC Licensees under the Small Business Investment Act (organization, control, permissible activities, conflicts, reporting, capital, and remedies). Targets Licensee conduct, corporate arrangements, transactions, and required filings with SBA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of management consulting services
rubrics_metrics.description: The words 'management consulting services' shall have the same meaning as the phrase 'consulting and advisory services' in section 308(b) of the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance through independent contractor
rubrics_metrics.description: Management consulting services may be performed through an independent consultant under contract with the Licensee, whether or not such consultant has similar contracts with other Licensees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records for management consulting charges
rubrics_metrics.description: A Licensee shall maintain a record for examination by SBA of the time spent and charges made with respect to management consulting services performed for each small business concern financed by the Licensee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such charges shall not exceed comparable reasonable charges by established professional non-Licensee consultants and consulting firms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization of wholly-owned subsidiary for consulting
rubrics_metrics.description: A Licensee may organize a corporation for the sole purpose of providing management consulting services subject to § 107.601.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All of its stock shall be owned and held by such Licensee; the parent-Licensee shall not sell, transfer or otherwise divest itself of any part of such stock, but it may transfer back any part thereof to the treasury of the wholly owned subsidiary whereupon such stock shall be retired and canceled. If the subsidiary is liquidated, its charter shall be surrendered and terminated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsidiary officers/directors requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each officer and director of the subsidiary corporation must be at the same time either an officer or director of the parent-Licensee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parent investment limits in subsidiary
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensee’s financial investment in its subsidiary corporation shall not exceed 1 percent of Licensee’s paid-in capital and paid-in surplus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advances and other receivables due the parent-Licensee by its subsidiary corporation shall not exceed 1 percent of Licensee’s paid-in capital and paid-in surplus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parent responsibility for subsidiary compliance and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The parent-Licensee shall be responsible for compliance by its subsidiary corporation with the Act and regulations; reports submitted to SBA by the parent-Licensee shall reflect consolidated figures covering activities of both corporations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The subsidiary shall make such separate reports concerning its activities as required by SBA; it shall be subject to examination and failure to make reports or submit to examination may be acted upon as an act of noncompliance on the parent-Licensee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Services to banks/other investors limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: A Licensee may render services for and compensation from banks or other investors or lenders only in connection with the financing of, or the providing of management consulting services to, a small business concern by the Licensee and in cooperation/participation with such bank or other investors or lenders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior SBA approval for transfers of control
rubrics_metrics.description: Transfer of control of a Licensee by any means shall be subject to prior written approval of SBA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior written approval is required in case of (1) a proposed transfer of 10% or more of the capital stock issued by a Licensee; (2) a proposed transfer resulting in acquisition of beneficial ownership of 10% or more; or (3) any proposed change in beneficial ownership which involves or results in a change in control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on consummating transfers without approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless prior written approval of SBA is obtained, no such transaction shall be consummated and neither the Licensee nor its officers, directors, employees or persons acting on its behalf shall register on its books any transfer of shares to the proposed new owner nor permit the proposed new owner to exercise voting rights or participate in conduct of Licensee’s affairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of transfer and related terms
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Transfer', 'stock transfer', or 'transfer of shares' refers to the aggregate amount of shares which any person or affiliated group transfers or undertakes to transfer during any six (6) month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Exercise of voting rights with respect to shares’ includes procuring or voting any proxy, consent, or authorization as to such voting rights. ‘Participation in the conduct of Licensee’s affairs’ includes access to, custody of, or control over corporate books, records, funds or other assets; participation in disposition thereof; or serving as officer, director, employee or agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transferors’ potential liability for violating approval requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: SBA may require the controlling shareholder(s) to enter into a written agreement assuming personal liability for a Licensee’s indebtedness to SBA, but only in the event of their direct or indirect participation in any violation of the prior approval requirements applicable to transfers of control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such personal liability will terminate if SBA subsequently approves the transfer of control and notifies the transferor(s) in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application filing and processing fee for transfer approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Application for prior SBA approval shall be promptly filed by the Licensee and by other parties in interest by appropriate written notice to SBA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application shall be accompanied by a processing fee of $100 for each officer, director, owner of 10% or more of Licensee’s stock, or other party involved, provided the fee shall not exceed $400 for any one transaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice and comment on proposed transfers
rubrics_metrics.description: SBA shall cause notice to be published in the Federal Register setting forth information concerning the filing of an application for approval of a proposed transfer of control, including names and location of Licensee and proposed transferees owning 10% or more, and shall provide interested parties an opportunity to submit written comments within a specified period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A similar notice shall be published in a local newspaper where the Licensee is located; a copy furnished to SBA within 10 days after such publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards SBA may impose in approving transfers
rubrics_metrics.description: SBA may condition approval on increased capitalization, assumption in writing by new owners of contractual liability for indebtedness, and other requirements deemed necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval shall be contingent upon full disclosure identifying real parties in interest, source of funds used to effect transaction, and such other data as SBA may request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting possible transfers of control
rubrics_metrics.description: The Licensee shall, upon obtaining knowledge thereof, promptly report to SBA the relevant facts pertaining to any transaction or event which affords reasonable grounds for belief that a transfer of control is involved or likely to occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If in doubt whether an event involves a change of control, resolve doubt in favor of reporting to SBA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common control restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: A Licensee shall not have an officer or director who at the same time is either an officer or director of any other Licensee (except a common manager approved in advance by SBA), nor shall 10% or more of the stock of any Licensee be owned or controlled, directly or indirectly, by an officer or director of or by any party owning or controlling 10% or more of another Licensee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirement for pledge of 10%+ shares
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever 10% or more of a Licensee’s stock is pledged or hypothecated as collateral and such pledge does not involve any transfer requiring prior approval, written notice setting forth the terms shall be furnished to SBA by the person making such pledge within 5 calendar days from the date of pledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensee subject to future Acts and regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: A Licensee shall be subject to all existing and future provisions of the Act and regulations issued thereunder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with other applicable laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Licensee shall comply with all applicable State or Federal law affecting its operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of securities from portfolio concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: A Licensee may retain its investment in a concern which qualified as a small business concern at the time of Licensee’s initial financing but which subsequently became large, subject to limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Securities of a large business received in connection with merger, consolidation, or affiliation may be retained as long as continued ownership does not interfere with Licensee’s ability to maintain adequate funds for financing small business concerns; Licensee may retain such securities until it has fully recovered original investment plus reasonable return. Additional financing only to honor commitments made while concern qualified as small or to protect original investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purchase of portfolio securities from another Licensee limit
rubrics_metrics.description: A Licensee may exchange with or purchase for cash from another Licensee portfolio securities acquired from small business concerns, but shall not have invested at any one time more than one-third of its total assets in such securities acquired through such exchanges or purchases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purchase is without recourse against the seller except liability from falsity of representations or warranties as to matters of fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensee limited to activities under the Act
rubrics_metrics.description: A Licensee shall engage in and conduct only the activities set forth in and contemplated under the Act and shall not engage in or conduct any other activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification as SBIC in communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Any written communication made by or at the behest of a Licensee shall identify that Licensee as 'a Federal Licensee under the Small Business Investment Act of 1958.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Idle funds handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Idle funds of a Licensee not employed in current financing and not invested per section 308(b) shall, without delay, be placed on demand deposit or in Time Certificates of Deposit maturing not later than 1 year after issuance in banks which are members of FDIC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Licensee may maintain an imprest petty cash fund not to exceed $500 at any one time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment adviser contracting and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: A Licensee may contract in writing with an individual or non-Licensee concern to serve on a continuing basis as its investment adviser; services shall be advisory only and shall not include actual performance of management or operating activities of the Licensee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensee shall furnish SBA a copy of such contract on or before the effective date; where Licensee is indebted to SBA, SBA reserves right to approve compensation. Two or more Licensees may contract with a common investment adviser with prior SBA approval. Contracts for appraisal, custodial, collection, bookkeeping, accounting, and legal services are not considered advisory services for these purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assets acquired in liquidation limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Where property is acquired by a Licensee in full or partial satisfaction of an obligation, Licensee may incur reasonably necessary expenditures for care and preservation of such property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except as permitted in writing by SBA, such expenditures (other than ordinary and necessary maintenance) plus Licensee’s funds attributable to such assets in liquidation shall not exceed an amount equivalent to Licensee’s investment limit under § 107.301(c). Licensee shall take steps to dispose of assets in liquidation within a reasonable period of time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bank further investment limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: A bank which holds 50% or more of any class of equity securities issued by a Licensee may make further investments only if such investments would not increase its percentage holdings of such securities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such capital increases shall be subject to SBA postapproval under § 107.1105.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on assuming control of small business concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither a Licensee, nor a Licensee and its Associates, nor two or more Licensees may assume control over a small business concern pursuant to management agreements, voting trusts, majority board representation, or otherwise, except as specifically permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption thresholds for control over a small concern
rubrics_metrics.description: Control will be presumed whenever a Licensee (or Licensee and Associates or two or more Licensees acting in concert) own, hold, or control, directly or indirectly, voting securities equivalent to: (1) 50% or more of outstanding voting securities if voting securities held by less than 50 shareholders; (2) 25% or more if voting securities held by 50 or more shareholders; or (3) a block of stock of 20% or more of outstanding voting securities which is as large as or larger than any other outstanding block of stock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This presumption may be rebutted by submission of appropriate evidence satisfactory to SBA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary control allowed only to protect investment
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensee may acquire temporary control over a small business concern only where assumption of control is reasonably necessary for the protection of Licensee’s investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divestiture plan requirement when acquiring temporary control
rubrics_metrics.description: A Licensee shall not assume control under the temporary control provision unless it has negotiated and entered into a fair and reasonable written plan at the time of financing, enforceable by the small concern or its shareholders, providing for relinquishment of control within a reasonable period not exceeding 7 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan shall state it is subject to SBA approval, shall be filed with SBA within 30 days after acquisition of control, be subject to SBA postapproval, and will be deemed approved unless Licensee is notified otherwise within 90 days after receipt by SBA. SBA may require renegotiation if plan appears inadequate; approval contingent upon full disclosure; approval may include conditions SBA deems appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual reporting on divestiture plan implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Licensee shall report to SBA in its annual financial report (SBA Form No. 468) a statement (in triplicate) setting forth current prospects for implementation of the divestiture plan and additional factors affecting status or feasibility of relinquishing control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renegotiation where changed circumstances affect divestiture plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Where changed circumstances indicate a workable arrangement no longer exists, SBA may notify and afford the Licensee and other parties an opportunity to submit evidence whether renegotiation of the divestiture plan should be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement action and divestiture interplay
rubrics_metrics.description: Divestiture plans shall not adversely affect or interfere with enforcement by the Licensee of its legal rights against a concern which has defaulted; if Licensee acquires control as a result of enforcement action, Licensee shall immediately notify SBA and take steps to divest itself of control within a reasonable period pursuant to an SBA-approved plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensee shall be free to negotiate with parties necessary to accomplish relinquishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existing plans compliance deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensees with control of a small business concern on the effective date must bring their divestiture plans into compliance not later than March 31, 1968, and provide for relinquishment within a reasonable period but not later than March 31, 1975; such plans to be filed with SBA not later than April 30, 1968.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans will be subject to SBA approval in accordance with this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission of divestiture plan after additional financing
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a Licensee assumes control and later provides additional financing to the concern, the Licensee shall within thirty (30) days resubmit its divestiture plan (amended if necessary) for SBA review and approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on voluntary capital decrease and treasury stock purchases
rubrics_metrics.description: A Licensee shall not voluntarily reduce its paid-in capital and paid-in surplus without prior written SBA approval. A Licensee may not purchase and hold more than 2 percent of any class of its stock without prior SBA approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mergers/consolidations/reorganizations require SBA approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to prior written approval of SBA, a Licensee may participate in a merger, consolidation, or reorganization with another Licensee or non-Licensee company where the resultant company will qualify as a Licensee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SBA's approval may be conditioned on such reasonable terms and conditions as it determines appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited uses of Licensee funds (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: No funds may be provided by Licensee for certain specified purposes listed in § 107.1001.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: relending/reinvesting by small business concern
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds may not be provided for relending or reinvesting by the small business concern, nor to concerns whose business activity involves investing, lending, factoring, purchase/discounting of debt obligations, or long-term equipment leasing with no maintenance/repair provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: financing other Licensees
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds may not be used, directly or indirectly, to purchase stock in or otherwise provide capital for a Licensee or to repay indebtedness to accomplish such purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: investments in unimproved real estate
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquisition or payment of obligations relating to prior acquisition of land or improved real estate to be held without prompt and substantial improvement or development for resale or leasing is prohibited, except where at least 59% of financing is used for improvement and improvement undertaken within 1 year from acquisition or financing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improvement/development deemed prompt and substantial if (1) amount equivalent to 59% or more of financing used for improvement/new construction/renovation and (2) undertaken within one year of acquisition or financing, whichever later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: purposes contrary to public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds may not be used for purposes contrary to the public interest, including gambling enterprises and activities, or any purpose encouraging monopoly or inconsistent with accepted standards of free competitive enterprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on foreign investment/use outside U.S.
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of funds outside the United States is prohibited except (1) for domestic production of products for distribution abroad or to acquire abroad materials, or (2) for use in branch operations abroad or transfer to controlled foreign subsidiary, provided major portion of assets and activities remain within U.S. jurisdiction after funds are so employed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: financing passive businesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds may not be provided to any person that is not engaged in a business operation conducted as a regular and continuous activity (passive businesses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: Licensee-associated supplier transactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds may not be provided to a small business concern which purchases goods or services from a supplier that is an Associate of the Licensee if 50% or more of the funds (or released funds) are used to purchase goods or services from such supplier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special restrictions where funds support alcoholic beverage enterprises
rubrics_metrics.description: Enterprises deriving a substantial portion of net sales from sale of alcoholic beverages (where such funds are proceeds of loans obtained from SBA) are restricted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within thirty (30) days after disbursement of any loan funds to Licensee, and thereafter while any part of such loan remains unpaid, the Licensee shall maintain assets consisting of cash, eligible Government obligations, and portfolio investments/loans not involving such alcoholic-beverage enterprises equal in face value to no less than the unpaid principal of such loan (exclusive of investments/loans already in portfolio at time of disbursement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: financing concerns primarily producing agricultural commodities
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds may not be used to finance concerns engaged solely or primarily in production of agricultural commodities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain unimpaired capital and definition of impairment
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Licensee shall maintain at all times an unimpaired capital. An impairment exists when the retained earnings deficit exceeds fifty (50%) percent of the private paid-in capital and paid-in surplus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treasury stock shall not be considered part of private paid-in capital and paid-in surplus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debtor Licensee notification threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: A debtor Licensee shall promptly inform SBA when its retained earnings deficit exceeds thirty-five (35) percent of its combined paid-in capital and paid-in surplus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of gains for capital impairment purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: For capital impairment purposes, gains may be recognized by SBA only to the extent permitted in Addendum II (Realization and Use of Income and Gains) to SBA’s Audit and Examination Guide (Revised Jan. 9, 1968).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Addendum II printed in Appendix 1 as part of these regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active operations requirement (inactive Licensees)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Licensee shall conduct active operations to meet financing needs in its area; inactivity constitutes a violation of regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of inactivity based on idle funds and financing activity
rubrics_metrics.description: A Licensee with more than twenty-five (25) percent of its assets in Idle Funds on March 31 shall be presumed inactive if it has not during the past 12 months provided new or additional financing aggregating at least 25% of an average of its said Idle Funds on such March 31 and the preceding September 30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It shall promptly file with SBA a written report setting forth reasons for inactivity. The presumption may be rebutted by appropriate evidence satisfactory to SBA.

rubrics_metrics.name: General conflict of interest prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-dealing to the prejudice of a small business concern, of a Licensee or its shareholders, or of SBA, is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: Licensee financing of its Associates
rubrics_metrics.description: Except where a written exemption is granted by SBA, a Licensee shall not, directly or indirectly, provide financing to any of its Associates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: reciprocal/related financing among Associates
rubrics_metrics.description: A Licensee shall not provide financing to an Associate of another Licensee if an Associate of the first Licensee receives, has received, or is about to receive any direct or indirect financing or commitment from such other Licensee or a third Licensee (including reciprocal or circular arrangements), except as may be exempted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on borrowing from portfolio concerns and related persons
rubrics_metrics.description: No Licensee or any of its Associates shall directly or indirectly borrow money from (i) a concern financed by such Licensee or (ii) an officer, director, or owner of 10% or more equity interest in such concern, or a close relative of such officer/director/owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on providing financing used to discharge obligations to Associates
rubrics_metrics.description: No Licensee shall directly or indirectly provide financing to a small business concern if the financing is used to provide funds to discharge or to free other funds for use in discharging an obligation of such concern to an Associate of the Licensee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parity of terms where both Licensee and Associate finance a concern
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a Licensee provides financing to a concern which also receives financing from an Associate of such Licensee within a period of 1 year prior or subsequent thereto, the terms of Licensee’s financing shall not be less favorable to the Licensee than those applicable to financing supplied by its Associate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensee shall retain written evidence of such financing by the Licensee and its Associate as part of its records available for SBA examination. Subparagraphs (4) and (6) do not apply to normal course transactions involving lines of credit or short-term financing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on Associates receiving fees or compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: No Associate of a Licensee shall receive, directly or indirectly, from a small business concern any fees or compensation in connection with financing supplied by the Licensee, or any money or thing of value for procuring, attempting to procure, or influencing Licensee’s action with respect thereto, except for bona fide services performed at the request of such concern and paid as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reasonable sum for necessary incidental services and costs (title exam, appraisal, credit report, survey, closing fees/expenses) may be collected by the Licensee and paid to an Associate for services actually rendered; such sum shall be approved by the Licensee and written evidence retained for SBA examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice prior to exemption granting for conflict transactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to an exemption being granted by SBA under conflict provisions, the Licensee shall publish in a newspaper of general circulation in the locality most directly affected by the transaction notice as specified by SBA and furnish a copy to SBA within 10 days after publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of 1940 Act company exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: A 1940 Act company granted an exemption by the SEC from applicable provisions of that Act for a transaction also subject to conflict provisions shall be exempt from the provisions here; provided the Licensee informs SBA of the SEC exemption and causes prompt public notice to be published in form specified by SBA and furnishes copy within 10 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of investment exception for Associates serving management roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensee may permit an Associate, employee, or representative to serve as officer, director, or in any capacity in management of a small business concern to protect its investment, provided the person has no other direct or indirect financial interest in the portfolio concern and has not served as officer/director/manager for more than 30 days prior to such financing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on disposing portfolio securities to Associates except by exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: Except where a written exemption may be granted by SBA, a Licensee shall not dispose of its portfolio securities to any of its Associates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a prerequisite to exemption, the Licensee must demonstrate that the terms of the proposed sale are no less favorable to it than are obtainable elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on selling portfolio securities to competitors
rubrics_metrics.description: Except where specifically approved in writing by the portfolio small concern not controlled by the Licensee or granted a prior written exemption by SBA, a Licensee shall not dispose of portfolio securities of a concern to a competitor of such small concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant particulars of all sales by Licensees of portfolio securities to competitors shall be promptly reported to SBA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess real estate investments grandfather rule for pre-1965 SBICs
rubrics_metrics.description: SBICs licensed prior to March 19, 1965, whose real estate investments as of March 31, 1965, exceeded one-third of their portfolio may retain such investments (if not in violation when made) but shall not undertake further real estate investments until portfolio diversified so real estate is less than one-third of total portfolio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thereafter, new real estate investments may be made as long as the one-third limitation is not exceeded and subject to § 107.1001(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: No Government sponsorship representation
rubrics_metrics.description: No Licensee in issuing any security shall represent or imply that such security has been approved by the United States or any agency thereof; a statement to that effect shall be included in any solicitations to investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violations: nonperformance of agreements with SBA
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonperformance by a Licensee of any of the terms, conditions, or requirements of any debenture, loan agreement, note, or other written agreement with SBA constitutes a violation of the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violations: false statements and material omissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any false statement knowingly made, or misrepresentation or failure to state a material fact necessary to make a statement not misleading in any document submitted by a Licensee to SBA pursuant to the Act or regulations, constitutes a violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examinations and reference to statutory authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Examinations of Licensees are governed by section 310(b) of the Act (see § 107.1101).

rubrics_metrics.name: Records and reports requirement (intro)
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensees are subject to requirements concerning records and reports (see § 107.1102).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific record-keeping and reporting obligations are provided elsewhere in the regulations (examples: management consulting records, consolidated reporting for subsidiaries, evidence of related-party financing, reports on divestiture plans, notification of transfers, annual financial reports SBA Form No. 468).
